## The problem

v3.1-interim could already refuse to *merge* on inference, but it still
flattened every recorded pair into `same_as`-shaped rows: a provable
copy of one upstream record and a purely inferential coincident pair
wore the same relation vocabulary, no site id travelled with a collapse,
and nothing re-verified a collapse after it landed — a stale or wrong
declaration could keep collapsing run after run.

## What landed — ruleset v3 (`camera_site_rules.toml` `version = "3"`)

- **`resolution/camera_sites.py`** — the C0/C1/C2/P vocabulary end to
  end:
  - **C0 `duplicate_target`** — one upstream layer ingested twice under
    one source, row- or byte-identical (the ADR-116 lineage evidence).
  - **C1 `namespaced_copy`** — the same normalised ref in ONE declared
    `id_namespace` inside ONE declared copy lineage (a `mirror`/`derived`
    `source_lineage_current` kind), the ref unique in each source's
    record set, within `copy_tolerance_m` (1.0 m), no suspected axis
    swap. Attribute *differences* on a copy are recorded in the collapse
    evidence (GQ-23), never silently reconciled.
  - **C2 `position_matched_copy`** (Q-L3-6 = a, `c2_enabled`) — a
    declared lineage carrying documentary evidence AND measured overlap
    ≥ `c2_min_overlap` (0.9) over ≥ `lineage_min_pairs` coincident pairs:
    bijective within `colocation_m`, ≤ copy tolerance, no attribute
    conflict.
  - **P `possible_duplicate`** — every inferential match (tiers 3/4/5),
    a namespaced-id miss, a soft conflict, a refused union, a shape
    alert, an axis-swap-suspected point, or a census-demoted pair:
    recorded with distance + reason + both site ids, **never merged**.
  - `_link_stamp` sets the emitted `relation_type` itself:
    `derived_from` for applied collapses (carrying the shared `site_id`
    — the cluster root subject id, never a minted entity;
    `merged_into` stays unwritten), `possible_duplicate` for
    proposed/refused pairs, `same_as` only for B5-certified or
    human-accepted edges, `cannot_link` for human rejects.
  - **GQ-25 in `_Clusters.refusal`** — a union that would put two
    different normalised ids of ONE declared namespace into one site is
    refused (`cluster_constraint:origin_distinct`); over-refusal stays
    conservative (over-counting, never under-counting).
  - **GQ-23 `derivation_census`** — runs after clustering on every run
    and re-verifies every applied C0/C1/C2 edge against the record set;
    a failure becomes a `CensusFailure` whose `(lineage-or-source,
    tier)` joins `demote_next_run`, consumed by the NEXT run's
    `cluster_decisions` (a consumed demotion is a run-key input — the
    demoted run is a new run, never a silent reuse) and surfaced as
    `possible_duplicate:census_demoted`. A stale declaration collapses
    for at most one run.
  - **axis-swap gate** — `axis_swap_suspected` (a current
    `geometry_defect=axis_swap` claim whose correction has not landed)
    is never a collapse input at assess, cluster, or census.
  - **`count_intervals`** (SIG-CONF-D05) — `upper` = post-collapse N;
    `lower` additionally folds every possible-duplicate link within the
    declared distance (`near_max_m`), nationally and per dossier.
  - **`m1b_sample_frame` + `clopper_pearson_lower`** — per declared
    namespace, a deterministic (run-key-seeded) sample of applied C1
    collapses with original/republish ids, shared ref and distance, and
    the exact one-sided bound the M-1b human re-check consumes.
  - `decide_auto_write_tiers` reconciled: `collapse_tiers` ride the
    census waiver (`eval_waived_tiers`); inferential tiers auto-write
    ONLY under a `certified_tiers` B5 certification — the committed
    agent/LLM gold labels can never certify one.
- **`camera_site_rules.toml`** — `version="3"`, the C0/C1/C2/P tier
  labels, `collapse_tiers={0,1,2}`, `inferential_tiers={3,4,5}`,
  `c2_enabled`, `c2_min_overlap`, `copy_tolerance_m`,
  `m1b_sample_size=200`, `candidate_auto_write={1,2}`.
- **`camera_site_gold.json`** — re-stamped `rules_version="3"` with an
  honest provenance entry: the 180 pairs are byte-identical agent/LLM
  labels (reference precision only; never an inferential certification).
- **`camera_sites_pg.py`** — reads `source_lineage_current`
  kind/evidence into `declared_details`; reads the latest completed
  run's `camera_site_demotion` into `demoted_collapses`; writes
  `relation_type` + `site_id`; appends the census row and demotion rows
  (PK conflicts = +0); feeds `geometry_defect`/`correction_reason` into
  the axis-swap gate; returns `demotions_consumed` /
  `census_recorded` / `demotions_recorded`.
- **`camera_site_review.py`** — `read_observation` re-tupled for the
  widened `_RECORDS_SQL`.
- **Additive sqitch `camera_site_derivation`** (deploy/revert/verify +
  plan) — `camera_site_match.relation_type` widens to the v3 vocabulary
  + new nullable `site_id`; NEW append-only `camera_site_census` (one
  row per completed run) + `camera_site_demotion` (`run_key,token,tier`
  natural key). `sig_materialize` SELECT+INSERT; `sig_export` SELECT —
  the camera-site machinery stays off the `public_read_allowlist`
  surface (its exact-set contract test caught the first draft's wider
  grant). The revert REFUSES when widened-vocabulary rows exist —
  append-only history is never falsified by a rollback. No UPDATE/DELETE
  on any living row.
